title: Sustainable poly(butylene succinate) films incorporating olive leaf extracts for active food packaging: biological, optical and thermal properties
content: The use of natural products impregnated into biodegradable polymers for active packaging has attracted considerable scientific interest due to their beneficial properties. In this context, olive leaf extract (OLE) and its hydrolysate (HYT) were incorporated into poly(butylene succinate) (PBS) to develop novel active packaging films. Oleuropein and hydroxytyrosol were identified, through LC-MS/MS analysis, as the main phenolic constituents in OLE and HYT extracts, respectively. Both extracts showed significant antioxidant activity, with IC50 values of 1.30 ± 0.04 and 0.68 ± 0.02 mg mL−1 for OLE and HYT, respectively. Both extracts exhibited antimicrobial activity, with HYT showing greater efficacy than OLE against the tested strains. The results also indicated that OLE and HYT addition into the PBS matrix did not induce a significant variation in the polymer's molecular structure and thermal properties. In contrast, changes in film color, thickness and transparency were noticed and discussed. PBS-OLE and PBS-HYT films preserved strawberry quality and reduced weight loss to 5–7% after 7 days, compared with 40% for the unpackaged control.
